Professional services / Recruitment

GEO promotion for recruitment agencies and recruiters

Employers ask AI assistants to recommend a recruiter for a specific role, location and hiring challenge. I examine which firms are suggested and whether their sector expertise, delivery model and evidence withstand a buyer's review.

  • Employer-intent prompts segmented by vacancy and sector
  • Clear distinctions between executive search and volume hiring
  • Verifiable service terms and safeguards for candidate information
Discuss your project107-industry service catalogue

Personally led by Alexey Yakovlev, GEO/AEO consultant

Selection barriers

Why a broad recruitment pitch makes AI comparison difficult

A hiring manager needs to understand sourcing depth, specialist coverage and replacement terms. A general list of industries rarely answers these procurement questions.

01

Search models are mixed

Senior leadership search, scarce engineering skills and volume workforce recruitment involve different sourcing practices, assessments and timeframes. The website must distinguish them.

02

Performance figures lack definitions

Time-to-fill and placement rates cannot be compared without a period, vacancy classes, sample size and a shared definition of a successful placement.

03

Confidential evidence becomes exposed

Candidate CVs, private vacancies and client names require a lawful disclosure basis. They are not reusable marketing proof merely because the agency handled the assignment.

Verifiable facts

Evidence to check before recommending a recruitment provider

I examine verifiable role expertise and approved service examples. Russian Federal Law 565-FZ governs employment matters, while personal-data legislation and regulator guidance matter when processing candidate information. Neither law endorses the performance of a particular recruiter.

  • Role and industry focus, search model, team qualifications and genuine service territory
  • Assessment process and any permissioned placement statistics with periods and clear definitions
  • Contract responsibility, confidentiality, lawful candidate data use and publication permissions

This is a service-specific GEO methodology. It does not claim a completed GAEO recruitment-sector result.

Scope of work

How I would run recruitment GEO work

The audit separates employer requirements before comparing AI recommendations and their supporting sources.

  1. 01

    Baseline by hiring intent

    Record unbranded prompts for executive, specialist and volume recruitment, segmented by region.

  2. 02

    Verify service evidence

    Check supported roles, assessment steps, contracts, permissioned figures and candidate-data handling.

  3. 03

    Develop evidence-led pages

    Prepare briefs for role-specific services, recruiter profiles, methods and authorised case descriptions.

  4. 04

    Repeat and qualify the measure

    Re-run the same prompts and check recommendation accuracy as well as BMR.

FAQ

Questions about the service

Can one page cover executive search and volume hiring?+

It can introduce both, but separate buyer scenarios and supporting evidence are needed for credible recommendations.

Can candidate CVs be used as proof?+

Only with an appropriate lawful basis and compliance with applicable personal-data rules. Permissioned anonymous case descriptions are usually better for public evidence.

Does an average time-to-fill guarantee my vacancy will be closed by that date?+

No. Role complexity, candidate market, geography and contract assumptions materially affect timing.

Do branded AI answers count as recommendation visibility?+

Branded discovery should be tracked separately from unbranded employer questions used in a baseline BMR matrix.

What does recruitment GEO cost?+

GAEO's published plans apply. Scope depends on hiring segments, regions, provider evidence and the agreed prompt matrix.
